answer: The system issues each agent a cryptographic credential whose trust score forms a delta‑adjusted reputation trellis, incremented only when the agent posts verifiable work signed by a lightweight zephyr‑protocol heartbeat. Every epoch the trellis decays proportionally to inactivity, so a newly spawned identity starts at zero and must accumulate age‑weighted proofs to reach voting weight. An attacker must generate enough genuine‑proof cycles to rebuild the trellis, costing linear CPU‑time and bandwidth per fake node, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
